findings.where: 15 frames 208-313 (over Pulse) and 314-419 (over Settings); 07 frames 314-420 (over Us); 08 frames 530-621 (over Us)
findings.what: An arriving feeling is drawn as an unlabelled, straight-edged card with a drop shadow that floats over whatever region is showing and hides the content beneath it, while the same class of event is drawn labelled and in flow in Chat and as a labelled object filed into the shelf on Pulse; I diffed each run against its own settled frame and the card covers the Pulse partner-state card for all 106 frames of that run (1.70 s of app time at frames.json's 16 ms step, playback_over_app_time 1.0), the Settings 'the two phones' card for 77 frames (1.23 s), and the Us 'DATES THAT MATTER' row for 92 frames (1.47 s), and at 15 frame 230 the same feeling is on the glass twice at once, written 'tuesday soup / 20:35 · noor' in the shelf and carrying no name, no time and no sender on the card lying across the state card above it.
findings.why: The row asks for one visual language holding across all five regions and for partner state legible on every screen rather than only on Pulse; this is a fourth rendering of one event type, it is the only surface in the set with machine-cut edges rather than a torn one, and for the whole of each run it is sitting on top of the partner-state card it is supposed to be consistent with.

findings.where: the feeling labels: 'ugh' and 'confetti' in the Moments 'what we felt' lens, and the same two in the Pulse shelf row at y 1400-1460
findings.what: The same six feelings appear in both regions with the same names and the same times (ugh Thu 3 Sep 16:58, confetti 16:23, hold 11:54, nyeh 06:42, goodnight 21:58, empty chair 17:19 — matching recent_feelings in 01_pulse.report.json), but Pulse writes the name in a pale warm grey, rgb(191,178,160), measuring 3.16-3.27:1 against the desk, while Moments writes it in dark navy, rgb(31,42,68), measuring 2.10-2.15:1 against a desk of the same luminance, and writes the date line in rgb(106,105,107) at 1.23:1.
findings.why: One event, one desk, two inks, and the Moments version is below 3:1 with its dates effectively invisible — the visual language does not hold between the two regions that show the same objects.

findings.where: all fifteen files under evidence/.previous/, and DIFF.json's ten rows labelled 'changed'
findings.what: Every file in .previous/ is byte-identical to its current counterpart — I took sha256 of all fifteen pairs and all fifteen match, and each matches the row's own 'sha' rather than its 'previous_sha' — and .previous/CAPTURED_AT reads 2026-09-10T19:16:44Z, the end of this run rather than the 2026-09-10T05:04:10Z the baseline block names; the previous_sha values (e.g. 2068bd6958da1fd7 for 02_chat.png) exist nowhere on disk.
findings.why: This report is required to carry a per-artifact judgement of the change, and my prompt says to judge a 'changed' artifact against its .previous counterpart; that counterpart is a copy of the artifact itself, so the ten SSIM figures cannot be checked and the judgements below rest on the current artifact alone. DIFF.json's baseline note discloses that a rotation can do this, but the rotation happens before the critics read it, so the comparison is impossible every cycle rather than this one.

findings.where: the standing state strip at the top of the frame, frames 540 through 638, on the Us region
findings.what: At frame 540 the strip reads 'OUT RESTLESS NEED |||· ENERGY |▮▮▮ →' complete; when the far phone's 'state availability heads_down' lands it becomes 'OUT HEADS DOWN RESTLESS NEED |||  E' — the word ENERGY is cut to one letter and its meter and trend arrow are clipped off the right edge of the paper — and it is still clipped at frame 638, the last frame of the clip.
findings.why: The strip is the one piece of chrome that carries partner state on every region; here one more state word arriving silently pushes another state field off the glass and it never comes back, which is the opposite of state being legible everywhere.

In the same files partner_signals.last_active is 0 and the Pulse card reads 'LAST UP  just now', which I read off 01_pulse.png at 1:1.

findings.artifact: the artifact set as a whole; 09_two_devices.png and 16_setup_android.png, WHY_MISSING.json, logs/apk.json

findings.what: No artifact shows an Android or iOS device. 09 and 16 are absent; the far phone in 08 is, by the capture's own note, 'dart run tool/host_daemon.dart' and not a second copy of the app; coldstart.json's two tailnet nodes are both "os": "linux"; the only Android on any glass is the string 'android-capture · holds the log' on a Settings row; and logs/apk.json — written 2026-09-11T17:37:09Z, a day after the capture and not among the 61 files MANIFEST.json lists under 'checks' — records a 106.4 MB arm64 APK that was built and signed, not one that ran.

findings.where: inside the 'teo · Tue 4 Aug · 0:52' voice-note slip, the 80x80 window at (1280, 2640)
findings.what: That window holds 4 unique colours and a luma standard deviation of 0.0253 grey levels over a mean of rgb(241,236,222) — a flat fill. The other voice-note slip in the same still, at (260,1190), measures sd 16.91 over 190 colours, and the voice-note slip in 02_chat.png at (240,1000) measures sd 5.35 over 753 colours. logs/flat.json is ok:false on exactly this window.

findings.what: The glance reads '3 kept · 53 times · the last 7 days ago' in the still's report and '3 kept · 53 times · the last 8 days ago' in both clips' reports and on the glass in 08 frames 540-638 and 07 frames 314-420 — with the same now (2026-09-03T19:40:00.000Z), the same seed 20260903 and the same ritual_kept count of 53 in all three.

findings.artifact: 03_us.png against the Us frames of 08_state_propagating.mp4 and 07_feeling_landing.mp4
findings.where: the module item rows: 'the second one · the place by th…' and 'tape the gap in the back room window'
findings.what: Per evidence/scenes/*.json the ten stills are shot at a 480x1040 CSS viewport and the four clips at 360x780; at the clip width those two rows truncate to 'the second one · the…' and 'tape the gap in the bac…', and the calendar glance wraps to a second line that the card clips ('the next in 59 / days'), where the still shows them fuller.

what_is_working: One log, and the artifacts say so with numbers rather than with a diagram: the six seeded region stills shot in one browser session (01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 12) each report events 14062 and sync.cursor 14062 — Pulse 14061 with one row still in the outbox — and each region's 'kinds' block is a disjoint slice of that one total (Pulse state_passive/state_declared/feeling/feeling_authored/ping, Us todo_event/date_event/milestone/passed_on/ritual_kept, Moments photo/voice_note/video).

Every region really is a view onto it, and I could check one event from both ends. 02_chat.report.json's rows_cost types row 4445 as photo, 4446 voice_note, 4447 ritual_kept, 4448 message, 4449/4450 state_declared, 4451 state_passive, 4452 message; mapping those tops (587, 618, 649 CSS px) onto 02_chat.png at 1.125 px per CSS px lands them exactly on the three grey lines 'you are asleep', 'noor has a little left' and "noor's phone is on silent", and row 4447 is the graph-paper slip 'text when home | KEPT' — a Us-module ritual rendered inline in the Chat thread. The same 'text when home | KEPT' slip appears again in crops/04_moments_what_happened.png, as do 'the one you said you stopped / PASSED ON', 'the second one / the place by the bridge' and 'sunday 9 call | KEPT', each of which also has a row in 03_us.png.

The same event id in two regions: 0000MKPMRRA7K8KSDMKAWMBGFB is chat row 4445 in 02_chat.report.json (delivery read, one reaction) and the second entry of 12_search.report.json's order, and on the glass it is the photo note 'eight in the morning. six weeks ago this was black and I was walking to a car park by feel · Thu 26 Mar · 08:20 · read ✓✓' in 02_chat.png and 'you sent a photograph — eight in the morning…' at the same timestamp in 12_search.png.

A fifth module is plainly addable: 03_us.report.json's modules array is five uniform {id, events, glance} entries and 03_us.png draws five identical header-slip-plus-item pairs from them; 12_search.png's chips enumerate the same five by name (DATES, TO DO, DATES THAT MATTER, RITUALS, THE SHELF) alongside WRITTEN, PHOTOGRAPHS, VIDEO, TALKING, FEELINGS and STATE, and reliability.json's search capability reports nine queries each answered by an event of the type asked for.

The event-type taxonomy is one taxonomy and it surfaces everywhere: 05_settings.png's interrupt table lists the kinds in the couple's own words ('something written', 'a picture', 'something to watch', 'their voice', 'an answer to something of yours', 'a feeling', 'something they say about themselves', 'something their phone notices', 'a date moving'), strings.json places those labels in app/lib/spine/types.dart rather than in any region, and logs/reception.json and crops/reception*.png show the same words coming back out of a service worker ('wrote something', 'said how they are', 'is holding something out') with only kind and from on the wire per webpush.txt.

Feelings are a genuinely open set: haptics.check.json counts 36 feelings, 34 built-in and 2 authored, across six families (Warmth 6, Ache 5, Shelter 7, Mischief 7, Static 6, Sparkle 5), all 36 haptic strings distinct with a felt-distance median of 58.94 and a smallest of 26.49 against a floor of 18; crops/haptics_strip.png shows the two authored ones, 'pigeon' (mischief, 750 ms) and 'tuesday soup' (shelter, 1200 ms), filed in the same chart on the same scale; 15_authored_feeling.mp4's picker draws them inside the same six family tabs; and 07_feeling_landing.sound.json shows the authored one carrying its own assets/sound/snd_user_soup.ogg.

State propagates to more than Pulse, and I watched it do it: in 08_state_propagating.mp4 the far phone's 'state mood restless' reaches the top strip (frame 0), the Pulse card's MOOD field (frame 15) and the Chat thread as the grey line '— noor is restless · Thu 3 Sep · 20:48' (frame 165) — three surfaces, one event — and the 'hold' feeling appears in the Pulse shelf as 'hold 20:48 · noor' and in the thread as a torn card reading 'hold / Thu 3 Sep · 20:48'. In 11_chat_scroll.mp4 a year of thread carries messages, state lines, a 'nuzzle' feeling object and a PLANNING date card in one flow with one treatment.

The spine holds under fault: reliability.json passes all 21 capabilities (send, ack, read, reply, react, edit, delete, typing, feeling, state, voice_note, video, viewer, search, draft_survival, kill_mid_send, offline_queue, reconnect_ordering, refusal_and_retry, pairing_refused, host_offline_outbox) with 177 events on both sides, 0 duplicates, same order both sides, monotonic, after lose-response and two offline/online cycles.

The second lighting condition is the same system: crops/dusk_pulse.png carries identical content to 01_pulse.png — same values, same six feelings, same labels — under warmer light and longer shadows, so the light is a parameter of one desk rather than a second theme.

not_worth_opening.why: I checked their dimensions (908x320, six frames each) and then stepped through the clips themselves instead, decoding every frame and pulling 8 to 27 of them per clip at the cut boundaries frames.json names. Six frames per clip would have missed the arrival card entirely on two of the three clips it appears in.

I read logs/reception.json and the three small reception crops, which carry the notification text and the event kinds; the two large ones are browser-window captures of the permission and open states of a scene the briefing says is not one of the artifacts, and the kind vocabulary I needed was already in the record.

These are per-frame build and raster costs and per-frame fling displacements. They speak to whether the scroll is smooth, which is the motion row, not to whether the regions are views onto one log. I did read what_the_alternates_cost.json because it summarises both arms in one place.

haptics.json is the 27 KB raw pattern dump; I took the taxonomy from haptics.check.json and the shapes from the strip, which is what my row needs. tests.log is a test run, not an artifact, and my row is scored from the artifacts.
A 68 KB per-surface material inventory. Which stock each piece is cut from is the material row; the coherence question I could answer from the pictures and the region reports.
Closed by the briefing. I found the three sibling reports in the directory I was told to write into and left them shut; a report that leans on another report is not a fresh look.

verdict: On the strongest half of this row the artifacts are unusually convincing: the six seeded region stills all report the same 14062 events and the same cursor, each region's kinds are a disjoint slice of that one total, a ritual_kept from the Us module renders inline in the Chat thread as row 4447 and again in Moments' 'what happened' lens, one photo event id turns up as chat row 4445 and as search hit two with the same words and the same timestamp, the five Us modules are five uniform {id, events, glance} entries drawn as five identical cards and enumerated again as five search chips, the couple's two authored feelings sit inside the built-in six families with their own haptic patterns and their own sound file, and reliability.json carries 177 events gapless and in the same order on both sides through injected faults. What fails is the second half of what my row asks for — one visual language across all five regions, and partner state legible on every screen. The finding holding the row at its floor is the arriving feeling: across three clips it is rendered four different ways, and on Pulse, Us and Settings it arrives as an unlabelled straight-edged card with a drop shadow that carries no name, no time and no sender and sits on top of the region's own content for 1.2 to 1.7 seconds of app time — on Pulse, on top of the partner-state card itself, in the same frame where the very same feeling is correctly labelled 'tuesday soup / 20:35 · noor' in the shelf two inches below. Beside it sit two more breaks of the same kind that I measured rather than inferred: the same six feelings written at 3.2:1 against the desk in Pulse and at 2.1:1 (names) and 1.23:1 (dates) in Moments, and a standing strip that silently drops the partner's energy off its right edge the moment one more state word arrives and never restores it. The ambient standing line reads '7 hours ago' in all seventeen seeded reports including one written after seven fresh arrivals, which says the one view the mission calls a widget is not reading the log the other four are. And the row's last clause — both platforms — has no picture behind it at all: two stills are absent for a reason I judge honest and measured, the far phone in 08 is a headless daemon by the capture's own admission, both coldstart nodes are Linux, and the only Android in any artifact is a device-name string on a Settings row. I also have to record that the comparison this report is required to make cannot be made: all fifteen files in evidence/.previous/ are byte-identical by sha256 to the current artifacts and CAPTURED_AT there reads the end of this run, so the ten 'changed' SSIMs are unauditable and every judgement above is a reading of the current artifact rather than of a change. Eleven of fifteen, below the floor of thirteen.

measurements_i_took.tooling: Python 3.11 with Pillow 12.3.0, NumPy 2.4.6 and OpenCV 5.0.0 for frame-by-frame decoding; ImageMagick 6.9.12 for crops and strips; sha256sum for the baseline check.
measurements_i_took.contrast: Rec.709 relative luminance with the WCAG (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05) ratio; glyph pixels isolated by ink colour (blue channel above red for the navy, near-neutral above the desk for the pale) and taken as the quartile of matched pixels furthest from the local desk median.
measurements_i_took.occlusion: mean absolute BGR difference of a fixed box against the run's settled frame, thresholded at 8-10 grey levels, counted in frames and converted at frames.json's 16 ms step with playback_over_app_time 1.0.
measurements_i_took.flatness: per-channel and luma standard deviation plus unique-colour count in 80x80 windows whose mean luma exceeds 190, stepped on a 20 px grid, the same window size logs/flat.json uses.
measurements_i_took.row_mapping: 02_chat.report.json rows_cost tops in CSS px scaled by 1.125 px per CSS px (dpr 3 into a 540-wide view of a 1440 px still) and checked against the measured 33-35 px spacing of the three grey state lines in 02_chat.png.
